column1: Figure 2: Sexual assault prevalence was significantly higher in the year ending (YE) March 2025 survey than a decade ago (YE March 2015)
Prevalence of sexual assault in the last year, among people aged 16 to 59 years, England and Wales, year ending March 2005 to year ending March 2025

column2:
1. No data are available for year ending (YE) March 2021 because the Crime Survey for England and Wales was suspended because of the coronavirus (COVID-19) pandemic. 
2. Data for YE March 2022 are not designated as accredited official statistics. Caution should be taken when using these data, because the quality of estimates may be affected by the reduced data collection period and lower response rates. 
3. Data for YE March 2023 are based on eight months of data collection because of an error in the survey, which resulted in missing data. Caution should be taken when using these data because of the impact of the reduced data collection period on the quality of the estimates. 
4. Data for YE March 2024 and YE March 2025 are based on a half sample. Caution should be taken because of the impact of the reduced sample size on the quality of the data. 
5. The categories “any sexual assault” and “rape or assault by penetration” include attempts.
Percentage of people aged 16 to 59 years who were victims once or more
